title: test(service-automation): pin the flow runAs and filter-date semantics hotcrm pins (two #15953 rows)
body:
Fixes #23604
Clause-②: no

## What this carries

The two `domain:services` rows split out of #15953's classification table (comment `6115219467`, rows as of slice 6's landing `6144431383`). Tests only, in `packages/services/service-automation/src/builtin/`. No production file changes. Each row is carried by the existing test file that already pinned part of it (ruling: the missing cases go in that file, not in a second file), and each file's header now names the row, #15953 and the hotcrm file it lets hotcrm retire (objectstack-ai/hotcrm#1583).

| row | hotcrm file it lets retire | carried by |
|:--|:--|:--|
| 8 | `test/readonly-write-semantics.test.ts` (its flow-writer rows: flow node, screen flow, subflow) | `crud-runas.test.ts` |
| 11 | `test/flow-filter-today-token.test.ts` | `crud-filter-guard.test.ts` |

### Row 8: a flow's `runAs` decides `isSystem` for its writes, per flow writer kind

- **Flow node: already pinned exactly.** `crud-runas.test.ts`'s first describe (`flow.runAs identity enforcement at the data layer (#1888)`) asserts that every data op of a `runAs:'system'`, `'user'` and default flow receives `isSystem` true, false and false. No new case. The header line names the hotcrm file.
- **Screen flow: added** (3 cases, one `it.each`). The screen parks the run, and nothing is written before it is answered. The `update_record` on the RESUMED leg receives `isSystem` from the flow's `runAs`: `'system'` gives true, `'user'` and omitted give false. The triggering user and org ride that write. The resume call carries no identity, so the write's context is the one the suspension persisted.
- **Subflow: added** (2 cases). The child is its own run, so the CHILD flow's `runAs` decides its writes, whichever way the two flows differ:
  - a `'system'` child under a default parent writes `isSystem: true` (actor `svc:flow:sys_child`), while the parent's own write stays `false`;
  - a default child under a `'system'` parent writes `isSystem: false` as the triggering user. The caller's elevation does not carry into the child.
- **Not this package's:** the PATCH and `beforeUpdate` writer kinds, and the objectql strip rule (an update strips `readonly` fields iff its context is not system). Those belong to the engine card.
- `runas-system-stamping.integration.test.ts`, `runas-attribution-contract.test.ts` and `runas-grant-resolution.integration.test.ts` pin attribution, row stamping and grant resolution. None of them pins the writer-kind switch, so none carries this row.

### Row 11: a flow filter's date value, in the dialect filters use now

The row names `interpolateFilter` resolving `TODAY()`. That function no longer exists: S6 (#19939) retired the template dialect from filter operands, the date macros included. This is what is true on `main`, measured and now pinned:

- **A CEL date envelope is evaluated before the query: added** (3 cases, one per CRUD verb). With the clock pinned at `2026-03-14T12:00:00Z` (only `Date` is faked), `{ $lt: { dialect: 'cel', source: 'isoDate(today())' } }` reaches the data engine as `{ $lt: '2026-03-14' }`, and `isoDate(daysAgo(30))` reaches it as `'2026-02-12'`.
- **`{today}` is passed through untouched: one operand added to the existing placeholder case** (`a query placeholder reaches the engine untouched, beside a literal`). That case already covered `{30_days_ago}`, `{current_year_start}` and `{current_user_id}`. `{today}` is a word of the query engine's vocabulary (`isKnownFilterToken`), which objectql resolves. The executor does not resolve it.
- **The retired `{TODAY()}` macro is refused before any query: added** (6 cases). At `registerFlow` the refusal points to the operand (`config.filter.close_date.$lt`) and names the CEL spelling `isoDate(today())`, and the flow is not registered. The executor's contract parse refuses it as a guard (`errorClass: 'guard'`), and the data engine receives nothing.
- **Not this package's:** objectql's `resolveFilterTokens`, which resolves `{today}` and refuses `{TODAY()}`. That belongs to the engine card.

The difference from the row's wording is the retired mechanism only. The date is still resolved before the query. It is now written as a CEL envelope instead of a `{TODAY()}` token, and `{TODAY()}` is now refused instead of resolved. No spelling was restored.

## Ablations (one per row)

Both mutations were temporary and were restored, with the restore proven, before any commit. Each went through `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs`: anchor count 1 to 0, replacement count 0 to 1, blob changed. A trap restored the file, and the restore was proven by the blob hash equalling HEAD's and an empty `git diff HEAD`. Both mutated files are imported by these tests through relative `./` paths, so vitest runs them from `src/` and no `dist/` build sits between the mutation and the run.

**Row 8.** `packages/services/service-automation/src/engine.ts:6351`, the run context's construction point:

```text
-            runAs: flow.runAs ?? 'user',
+            runAs: 'user',
```

`crud-runas.test.ts`: `Tests  8 failed | 21 passed (29)`. The new cases that went red:

- `screen flow, runAs:'system': the write on the resumed leg is isSystem true`: `AssertionError: the screen flow's runAs did not decide the resumed write: expected false to be true`
- `subflow: a 'system' child called by a 'user' parent writes elevated; ...`: `AssertionError: the 'system' child's runAs did not decide its write: expected false to be true`
- `subflow: a child with no runAs called by a 'system' parent writes as the user ...`: `AssertionError: the 'system' parent's own write was not elevated: expected false to be true`
- plus the five existing elevation cases, e.g. `REGRESSION: a runAs:'system' flow must reach the data layer elevated (fails if runAs is ignored)`: `runAs:system did not elevate the data op (#1888 regressed): expected false to be true`.

Stayed green, as predicted before the run: the `'user'` and omitted screen cases, because the mutation produces exactly their answer. This mutation reddens the second subflow case at its parent assertion, so it never reaches that case's leak assertion. A mutation that makes the child inherit the caller's `runAs` would redden the leak assertion. It was not run, because the ruling allows one ablation per row.

**Row 11.** `packages/services/service-automation/src/builtin/crud-nodes.ts:88`, in `resolveNodeFilter`:

```text
-        if (!isExpressionEnvelopeShaped(operand.value)) continue;
+        if (true) continue;
```

`crud-filter-guard.test.ts`: `Tests  20 failed | 17 passed (37)`. The new cases that went red: `get_record`, `update_record` and `delete_record: a CEL date envelope is evaluated before the query — the engine receives the date`, each with:

```text
-     "$lt": "2026-03-14",
+     "$lt": { "dialect": "cel", "source": "isoDate(today())" },
-     "$gte": "2026-02-12",
+     "$gte": { "dialect": "cel", "source": "isoDate(daysAgo(30))" },
```

Stayed green, as predicted: the six `{TODAY()}` refusal cases and the placeholder case, which do not depend on evaluation. The refusal is the spec's judge, `classifyFlowFilterOperandString`, composed into the node contract. That judge lives in `packages/spec` and is not this row's ablation.

## Tests (head `aed1c7c3fd`)

- Dependency closure built first: `turbo run build --filter='@objectstack/service-automation^...' --concurrency=2`, 29 of 29 tasks successful.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/service-automation exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2`: `Test Files  186 passed (186)`, `Tests  2500 passed (2500)`.
- The two edited files alone: `Test Files  2 passed (2)`, `Tests  66 passed (66)`. The slowest new case took 12 ms.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/service-automation run typecheck` exited 0. The test program (`tsconfig.test.json`) lists both edited files, and `check:test-typecheck` reported 0 errors.
- `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack` (2 paths, +260/-3) derived 52 commands. 51 exited 0. `pnpm check:dual-build-cjs-loads` exited 3 (`PREREQUISITE NOT MET`: it reads the built output of every workspace package, and only this package's closure is built here), so it is NOT MEASURED locally and CI's run is the measurement. `--ran` reconciliation: `52 derived famil(ies) accounted for — 51 run, 1 NOT-MEASURED`.

## Acceptance notes

- The card body's row 11 names a retired mechanism (`interpolateFilter`, `TODAY()`). The semantics it stood for are pinned in today's dialect, described above. The premise survives, with the mechanism updated.
- The PM's lead for row 8 named the three `runas-*` files. The flow-node switch is actually pinned in `builtin/crud-runas.test.ts`, which is why the new writer-kind cases live there.
- `registerFlow` refuses a value-slot token by throwing a bare `Error` whose message is the located refusal, with no `code`. The existing pins and the new ones therefore assert the message's located prefix (built from the exported `VALUE_SLOT_TEMPLATE_REFUSAL`) and the named CEL spelling. This is an observation about an in-process API, not a finding: carrier none.
